statements.statement: Voltage is what actually damages your body when you get an electrical shock.
statements.explanation: It is current (amps) that does the damage, not voltage. Voltage is the push that forces current through your body's resistance, but the current itself causes the harm.

statements.statement: As little as 0.1 amps through the heart can be fatal.
statements.explanation: 0.1 amps is a tiny amount of current, but it is enough to disrupt the heart's electrical signals and cause death.

statements.statement: Higher voltage can force more current through your body's natural resistance.
statements.explanation: Your body has natural resistance. Higher voltage provides a greater push, overcoming that resistance and allowing more current to flow through you.

statements.statement: If the voltage is low enough, no dangerous current can flow through your body regardless of conditions.
statements.explanation: At very low voltages, your body's resistance is high enough that virtually no current can be pushed through. This is why low-voltage hobby electronics are safe to touch.
